thread:
jess: Hey team — getting multiple reports from a single customer that p95 and p99 latency jumped after we onboarded tempest-30b-v2 yesterday. Root request is a streaming chat call with ~12k tokens context. Anyone else see this?

matt: saw a blip in the infra dashboard around 10:45 UTC, coincides w/ the model push. p95 up from ~220ms to ~720ms for that tenant, p99 to ~1.8s.

kevin: thanks — do we know if it's KV cache misses or tokenizer slowdown? New model changed tokenizer recipe last minute, right?

jess: yes, tokenizer changed. customer mentioned a spike when sending large system prompts + long conversation history. They reproduced locally with our SDK.

lina: tagging @sre-bot for traces. can you pull a trace for one of the slow requests?

sre-bot: Attached trace id: trace-20260305-8943. Top span shows heavy time in tokenization and model input preproc (approx 1.1s), then a longer decode loop due to attention kernel fallback (~600ms).

oliver: interesting — kernel fallback might happen if sequence length > 8192 for that model quantization path. tempest-30b-v2 default context is 64k, but our optimized kernels only handle up to 16k without special compilation. did onboarding set the 64k runtime config?

matt: yes, packaging set runtime.context_max = 65536 to advertize long context. but we didn't ship the long-context optimized kernels for the 30B opt variant. fallback to generic kernels is likely.

jess: customer repro steps (from them):
```
# reproducible minimal repro (python)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., model='tempest-30b-v2')
with open('long_prompt.txt') as f:
    prompt = f.read()  # ~12k tokens
resp = client.chat.stream(prompt)
```
They also included a tokenized size: 12234 tokens.

kevin: that explains kernel fallback. Also tokenizer change: new BPE merges increased token counts in some edge cases (long system + conversation) — 12k tokens might map to more byte-level work in the tokenizer. Combined effect is tokenization CPU + fallback GPU slowdown.

lina: mitigation path options: 1) rollback context_max advertise to 16k for hosted until kernels are compiled, 2) hotfix to guard route: if token_count > 16k route to dedicated pool with long-context kernels, 3) provide a temporary client-side transform to chunk history and stream with KV-friendly segments.

matt: ops note — rolling back context_max would be quick (config push), low risk, but will break customers expecting 64k. Hotfix routing needs policy update but safer.

jess: customer is OK with temporary slowdown but wants ETA. Can we get kernels compiled in next 48h?

kevin: compile + validation for this quantized variant takes ~24-36h if we prioritize. Testing across sample sequences (including pathological tokenization) is required.

oliver: short-term mitigation: implement route-by-token-count. we have the routing hooks in smart-router; just need a policy: if model=="tempest-30b-v2" and token_count>16384 then route to long-context pool. Will need a quick rollout with canary.

lina: I'll put together the routing policy patch and a canary (5%) for a single region. also adding a temporary metric alert: model.tempest-30b-v2.tokenizer_cpu_ms and .kernel_fallback_count.

jess: for support reply: tell customer we're aware, root cause is tokenizer + unavailable long-context kernels causing fallback; we have a mitigation rolling out (routing by token_count) and a kernel build in progress. ETA ~48h. Offer to whitelist them into canary for earlier fix.

matt: ops checklist:
- [ ] create routing policy PR -> @oliver
- [ ] enable canary 5% us-west -> @lina
- [ ] start kernel compile with perf tests -> @kevin
- [ ] add tokenization telemetry to ingestion -> @lina
- [ ] draft support message + RCA -> @jess

kevin: one more note — tokenizer change also affects embedding and reranking endpoints. recommend scanning top customers with heavy long-context usage and preemptively offering canary.

oliver: putting PR for routing policy up in 15m. will include automated rollback if p99 improves < 20% within first hour.

sre-bot: Canary deployment succeeded: canary-id canary-1768010300, 5% traffic, us-west-2. Initial telemetry: p95 down from 720ms -> 260ms for canaried requests.

jess: great, update customer: can offer immediate canary opt-in. They want opt-in. Moving to support with next steps.

lina: created alert dashboard link: https://console.redwood/infr/dash/tempset-30b-v2-tokenization (bookmark). will monitor for the next 24h.

matt: postmortem action items: (1) include tokenizer regression tests in model onboarding checklist, (2) require long-context kernel validation before advertising context_max>16k.

jess: thanks everyone. sending the support note now and offering canary. will follow up after kernel build completes. :thumbsup:

oliver: FYI — I'll add a small client-side SDK helper to estimate token_count early and warn users before they send enormous system prompts. might reduce accidental hits.

kevin: timeline update: kernel build queued, estimated finish 28h. I'll ping here when artifacts ready.

jess: closing the thread for daily sync; will reopen if anything changes.
